Meaning of thermal equilibrium and Zeroth law of thermodynamics
Thermal equilibrium as a working principle of a mercury thermometer

card.title: Exam bank — every board question on heat and temperature

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Four questions: Zeroth law plus why 'zeroth' (2023), faulty-thermometer correction (2023: -5/105 scale), heat-vs-temperature twice (2022, 2021). Heat is transit energy (joule); temperature is mean molecular kinetic energy (kelvin); equilibrium transitivity founds thermometry.

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: Q (J) vs T (K) · faulty scale: T = (R - lower)/(upper - lower) x 100 C · K = C + 273.15

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Equilibrium needs sustained thermal contact (why thermometers wait). The Zeroth law's transitivity requires all three pairwise contacts thermal. Faulty-scale correction assumes linearity between fixed points (meaning uniform bore, linear expansion).

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: -5/105 thermometer: slope 110/100 = 1.1, true T = (R+5)/1.1; liquid at true 40 C reads 39 C. Heat-vs-temperature repeats across years because the confusion persists: transit vs state, extensive vs intensive, joule vs kelvin.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: NEB 2023 (2): Zeroth law (A~B, B~C implies A~C) plus naming history (named after 1st/2nd, logically prior). NEB 2023 (3): T = (R+5)/110 x 100. NEB 2022/2021 (2): heat (J, transit, extensive) vs temperature (K, hotness, intensive) table.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Mark-losers: calling heat a state quantity; kelvin vs Celsius in scale math; 'zeroth' unexplained. Thermometers disturb tiny systems (finite heat capacity) — equilibrium includes the instrument.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: Equilibrium as equivalence relation (reflexive, symmetric, transitive) — transitivity IS the Zeroth law, isotherms are its classes. Linear-scale correction derives from two-point calibration (ice, steam) with uniform-bore assumption.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: 'Why zeroth' means named-later-logically-first, one line. Faulty thermometer: (R-lower)/(upper-lower) x 100. Heat-vs-temperature: J-vs-K plus transit-vs-state table.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: NEB 2023 (2): Zeroth law + naming. NEB 2023 (3): -5/105 faulty scale. NEB 2022 (2) + NEB 2021 (2): heat vs temperature + SI units.
